personal.name: Michael Swartz
bio: I'm doing my Honours in Computer Science at Stellenbosch. My research is on Text-to-SQL: how well quantised open-source models, from 1.5B to 32B parameters, translate a question into SQL, and what it actually costs to make them correct themselves.

Most of what I build sits close to that — running models locally, agentic tooling, and the infrastructure to keep both alive on one machine. I like the parts where a model has to work out that it was wrong.

research.title: Error-aware Text-to-SQL for low-resource LLMs
research.description: A benchmarking pipeline that evaluates open-source models from 1.5B to 32B parameters on BIRD, sorts their failures into syntax, schema, semantic and logic errors, and feeds them back for iterative self-correction. Correction runs as a chain — deterministic parsing and schema checks first, an LLM only as a last resort, capped at three rounds per query. I introduced Mean Correction Iterations to measure how much correction effort each point of accuracy costs. The bottleneck turned out to be detection rather than repair: without a reference answer, the classifier misses about 41% of semantic errors.

research.title: Next
research.description: Applying for Master's funding to work on that detection bottleneck: fine-tuning models to diagnose their own output, finding confidence signals that don't need a reference answer, and turning MCI into something useful at deployment time.

projects.title: Claude Code skill for the Lengau cluster
projects.description: A skill that Claude Code works from to run my experiments on the CHPC's Lengau cluster — the VPN, PBS Pro jobs, a CPU-only Ollama built from source, and handoff notes that pass state between sessions on different machines. Needed because nothing about the cluster is standard: the compute nodes have no outbound internet and everything runs inside Singularity containers.

projects.title: Multiplayer table soccer
projects.description: Foosball in the browser, built in a week. Vanilla JS and Socket.IO with no frameworks, which is what made the real-time state — powerup timers, spectators joining mid-game — the hard part. Deployed to Cloudflare Workers through GitHub Actions.

projects.title: repo-skill-finder
projects.description: Scans a repo's tech stack, matches it against a skills registry, flags what's missing, and generates the missing skills.

projects.title: PDF automation suite
projects.description: Three tools for filling PDF forms nobody made fillable: OpenCV finds the underlines and blank fields, a writer places typed responses without breaking alignment or spacing, and the whole thing saves out automatically.

projects.title: Multi-room chat application
projects.description: A Java chat app with multiple rooms, live broadcasting, real-time voice calling, end-to-end encryption and integrated torrenting for file sharing. Mostly an exercise in networking and threading.

projects.title: Laser tag
projects.description: Mobile laser tag that uses the phone camera and computer vision to detect players and register hits.

projects.title: Appa Mod
projects.description: A Forge 1.20.1 Minecraft mod, co-developed, adding a rideable flying mob.

projects.title: File converter
projects.description: A PyQt6 desktop app for bulk conversions — folders of images into a PDF, and similar — with GitHub Actions building the macOS binaries.

projects.title: Pose detection in the browser
projects.description: Real-time human pose detection with TensorFlow.js, including the Safari-specific debugging that came with it.

projects.title: Binary sort in x86 assembly
projects.description: A full binary sort written in 32-bit NASM with a C interface for testing, working with structs and low-level optimisation.

projects.title: AirRace
projects.description: A strategic card game with an AI solver. Got 120%, including full marks for the AI.

earlier: Before that, the usual learning projects — a Pokémon clone in vanilla JS with a map built in Tiled, solitaire and blackjack in Pygame, snake, an eye tracker that follows the cursor.
